subject: Mutual Action Plan: Performance evaluation & quantization kernel analysis
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Park <diane@orbitai.com>, procurement@orbitai.com
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: Performance evaluation & quantization kernel analysis

Hi Diane / OrbitAI team,

Thanks again for the sync today — great to align on scope. Attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_OrbitAI_v1.xlsx) and a starter kernel profile export (kernel_profiles_202607.csv). Summary of what we propose for the MAP and evaluation window: 

- Objective: validate production latency / throughput and quantization viability across typical OrbitAI workloads and decide on model variant + rollout plan.
- Key metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), tokens/sec throughput, memory footprint, and per-kernel call counts.
- Targets (proposed): P95 <= 150ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens), TTFT <= 120ms median, concurrency tests at 50/200/500 simultaneous sessions.
- Quantization matrix: FP16 (baseline), BF16, INT8 (per-layer), INT4 (experimental). Verify kernel-level regressions and operator fallbacks.
- Timeline (recommended): 2-week evaluation window (smoke + quant runs + regression checks) followed by a 1-week canary deployment if results pass.

Ask from your side: confirm a preferred test window (we can run in us-west region), share credentials for the test S3 bucket or a sample dataset (or we can run synthetic workloads if that’s easier), and confirm the workload mix (short vs long prompts).

Attachments: MAP_OrbitAI_v1.xlsx (action items + milestones), kernel_profiles_202607.csv (starter kernel op list).

We’ll follow up with a detailed test matrix tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Diane — thanks, this is helpful. I’ve sketched a concrete test matrix below and attached a cleaned kernel export. Please review and tell us if we should tweak concurrency or sequence length bins.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
- Day 0 (smoke): environment validation, model load, baseline FP16 run, verify telemetry.
- Days 1–4 (quant experiments): run FP16 (baseline), BF16, INT8 (per-channel), INT8 (per-tensor), INT4 (experimental) across sequence length bins [0-64, 65-256, 257-512, 513-1024].
- Days 5–8 (throughput/concurrency sweep): concurrency levels [50, 200, 500]; batch sizes [1, 4, 16]; measure tokens/sec and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Days 9–10 (regression checks): run the eval-suite (semantic-similarity and safety checks) against canned prompts + a human-reviewed goldset. Drop threshold: semantic-similarity delta > 1.5% flagged.
- Days 11–13 (stability & repeatability): rerun top candidates, collect kernel trace & perf counters.
- Day 14 (handoff): consolidated report + recommended rollout plan.

Metrics collected: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, peak GPU memory, kernel dispatch counts, operator fallbacks, and qualitative eval-suite scores.

We can run the quantized variants from Redwood’s Private runner inside your account (preferred) — requires short-lived IAM role we can assume. If OrbitAI prefers to run, we’ll provide deterministic config and scripts.

Attachments: kernel_profiles_202607.csv (operator names, frequency, sample durations).

Next step: confirm the test start date (we have capacity the week of 2026-07-27) and I’ll post a calendar invite including a 30-min runbook walkthrough.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

Mike / team — noted. Short answers:

- Compliance: I’ve attached a short link to our compliance pack in the MAP and will share SOC2 artifacts with your security contact (we can provide a signed NDA if required).
- Cost estimate: based on the proposed matrix and running in us-west, expect ~480 GPU-hours for the full sweep (ballpark). We can cap trial spend at $12k — let us know if OrbitAI prefers a lower cap.
- Regression & rollback: primary safety measure is maintaining an FP16 (or BF16) fallback. Our regression checks are automated via the eval-suite — we’ll flag any semantic-similarity delta > 1.5% or latency regressions where P95 increases > 20% vs baseline. If a candidate quantized variant fails, we move to the prior-approved model and halt rollout.

I’ve added a short appendix in the MAP with the signoff gates and acceptance criteria (see attached latency_throughput_plots.pdf for example outputs from a prior customer).

Please confirm: signoff on the test window starting 2026-07-27 and trial budget cap. Once confirmed we’ll schedule the runbook walkthrough.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Team — thanks for the fast turnaround and alignment. Final check and action items from Redwood: 

1) Start date: aim to start the evaluation on 2026-07-27. Redwood will run in us-west in OrbitAI’s account (we’ll share a short-lived IAM role and an S3 presigned flow).
2) Trial cap: set at $12k as proposed. We will not exceed this without explicit written approval.
3) Technical plan: follow Priyom’s test matrix. Primary goal is to identify quantized candidates that meet OrbitAI’s P95/TTFT targets with minimal semantic drift.
4) Regression policy: automated flag if semantic-similarity delta > 1.5% or P95 degrades > 20% vs FP16 baseline. On flag: immediate rollback to FP16 and a joint postmortem.
5) Deliverables by Day 14: consolidated MAP status, kernel-level anomalies (ops with >5% fallback rate), latency/throughput plots, and a recommended rollout candidate (or fallback decision).

Please reply with a single-line signoff ("Start on 2026-07-27, cap $12k") or propose edits by EOD 2026-07-23. Once we have a signoff I’ll drop the calendar invites and runbook doc.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & GTM | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
